prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, audience, and preferred services. I can help you find the best fit. A few quick questions so I can recommend specific agencies:

- What type of healthcare organization are you? (hospital system, clinic, private practice, specialty practice, medical device, pharma, payer, health tech/startup)
- Which services do you need most? (branding, digital/SEO, paid media, content, PR, physician marketing, patient acquisition, analytics, marketing automation)
- What’s your annual marketing budget (range)?
- Are you committed to a local St. Louis agency, or is a national agency with healthcare expertise acceptable?
- Timeline and KPIs: launch a campaign now, ongoing support, or one-off project? What success metrics matter most (leads, appointments, admissions, brand awareness, patient retention)?

If you’re not sure yet, here’s a practical way to evaluate agencies and some questions to ask them:

Evaluation criteria
- Healthcare experience: relevant case studies and measurable outcomes in your sub-sector
- Strategic capability: evidence of strategy, not only tactics
- Digital competence: SEO, paid search, social, content, analytics
- Compliance experience: HIPAA, FDA (if applicable), healthcare regulations
- Measurement and reporting: clear KPIs, attribution, dashboards
- Team and culture fit: will they integrate with your internal team?
- References and results: references from similar clients and metrics (CPL, CAC, conversions)
- Budget fit and transparency on fees

Key interview questions
- Tell me about 2–3 healthcare projects like ours and the outcomes (metrics).
- How do you handle regulatory and privacy requirements for healthcare marketing?
- Who will be on our account day-to-day and what are their backgrounds?
- How do you measure campaign ROI and attribution?
- What is your approach to patient acquisition vs. physician/provider recruitment?
- Can you provide references I can contact?

Contract and engagement tips
- Start with a pilot project (3–6 months) to prove results before committing long-term.
- Require clear KPIs and a reporting cadence in the contract.
- Include an exit clause and IP ownership clarity for creative/assets.

If you want, tell me your answers to the questions above and I’ll:
- Recommend 3–5 St. Louis agencies (or national agencies with local presence) that fit,
- Provide a side-by-side comparison and recommended next steps, and
- Draft an RFP or interview script you can use.

Which option would you like to do?
